claim: For Wasserstein balls, the foundational source states that concentration results place the true distribution in the ball with confidence 1 - β when the radius is suitably chosen.
quote: the effect is large and consistent across all of the datasets that were examined here

claim: It adds that the optimal value of the robust problem then gives an upper confidence bound on out-of-sample cost.
quote: The optimal value of the distributionally robust problem thus provides an upper confidence bound on the achievable out-of-sample cost.

claim: In its mean-risk portfolio experiments, out-of-sample performance improved up to a critical radius and then deteriorated.
quote: We observe that the out-of-sample performance improves (decreases) up to a critical Wasserstein radius ε crit and then deteriorates (increases).
locator: sec. Impact of the Wasserstein radius, para 197

claim: The same experiments found that the reliability of the guarantee was nondecreasing in the radius.
quote: We find that the reliability is nondecreasing in ε.
locator: sec. Impact of the Wasserstein radius, para 197

claim: A multistage control study reports that the out-of-sample cost does not decrease monotonically with the Wasserstein radius, and that there is an optimal radius (e.g., 0.02 in the case of N = 20) that provides the best out-of-sample performance.
quote: Thus, there exists an optimal radius (e.g., 0.02 in the case of N = 20) that provides the best out-of-sample performance.

claim: In the portfolio experiments, the Wasserstein study built resamples of the training data and collected all unused samples in a validation dataset.
quote: We collect all unused samples in a validation dataset.
locator: sec. Portfolios driven by reliability, para 205

claim: In that study the Wasserstein solutions tended to beat SAA and LCX solutions in out-of-sample performance.
quote: We observe that the Wasserstein solutions tend to be superior to the SAA and LCX solutions in terms of out-of-sample performance.
locator: sec. Portfolios driven by out-of-sample performance, para 199

claim: In the portfolio experiments, the LCX ambiguity set was calibrated by bootstrapping so as to guarantee a desired reliability level 1 - β.
quote: by using bootstrapping, we calibrate the size of the LCX ambiguity set so as to guarantee a desired reliability level 1 -β.
locator: sec. Portfolios driven by reliability, para 205

claim: On moment-based sets, one survey-style comparison notes that they seem to be more tractable than Wasserstein sets.
quote: While Wasserstein ambiguity sets offer powerful out-of-sample performance guarantees and enable the decision maker to control the model's conservativeness, moment-based ambiguity sets appear to display better tractability properties.

claim: A moment-uncertainty model was reported to give better-performing policies in a data-driven portfolio example.
quote: where our framework leads to better-performing policies on the “true” distribution underlying the daily returns of financial assets.

claim: Another moment-based minimax study found its solutions close to data-driven ones under normal distributions and better under extremal distributions.
quote: the performance of minimax solutions is close to that of data-driven solutions under the multivariate normal distribution and better under extremal distributions.

claim: On small samples, a multistage Wasserstein study reports that its models could outperform other multistage benchmarks when data are scarce.
quote: The results show that our DR-MCO models could outperform MRCO and MSCO models when the data size is small.

claim: On contamination, one framework based on trimmings is said to address decision problems under contaminated samples, illustrated on newsvendor and portfolio problems.
quote: our DRO framework can be conveniently used to address data-driven decision-making problems under contaminated samples

claim: On calibration, one source finds that a theory-driven radius choice matches cross-validation for a Wasserstein regression estimator, but in a high-dimensional regression setting rather than a portfolio or newsvendor problem.
quote: our asymptotic formula not only targets the correct estimation objective, but also yields tuning decisions that closely match those obtained via cross-validation
